reason: The broadening thesis is doing its job in exactly the tape it was built for. In the 10-14 to 10-16 semiconductor selloff, SMH fell from about 632 to 540 (-15% since the 10-05 entry) and SPY lost about 2%, while RSP (+1.4%), COWZ (+4.0%) and XLE (+7.6%) are up on the leg. This is the equal-weight/value-over-mega-cap rotation the book was meant to capture. GDX and GLD came back from the 10-14 dip (GDX 83.40 to 87.71) and sit just above entry, and no leg is within 10 points of its stop. The weakest legs are SIL -4.2% against a -22% stop and XLI -1.4%. XLI's AI-capex-spillover link is now under some pressure, but a 1.4% dip does not break the thesis, and a full or partial rebalance would cost real basis points for no change in view. Research note: web search returned nothing dated October 2026, so this rests on daily closes I pulled from Yahoo Finance (SPY, SMH, RSP, GDX, GLD, XLE, XLI, KRE, the 10y/30y yields and DXY), not on news coverage.
